_status: Practice, not law. The bye-laws set a room's area and width; they do not say a bedroom must hold a bed. Every figure here is a planning convention and is marked unverified for that reason, not because a clause is waiting to be read.
_why: A room can pass every legal minimum and still not be usable. The JP Nagar 40x60 drew a 6'3" x 15'6" kitchen, a 7'3" x 15'6" dining room and an 8'1" x 15'6" hall: each above its area, width and aspect limits, and none of them holds its furniture the way a person would place it. Minimums are legal floors; this is the size a room needs to be lived in.
_how: Each room kind lists one or more arrangements. An arrangement is what must fit ACROSS the room and ALONG it, wall to wall, inside the plaster. An entry is either a fixture from refine_v1.fixtures with the side of it that lies in that direction, so the furniture drawn is the furniture fitted, or a clearance in metres with what it is for. A room is usable when its clear rectangle holds ANY one arrangement, turned either way. Short of every arrangement, stage 5 prices the shortfall and stage 7 reports it; nothing is refused, because a legal room is not an illegal one.
_scope: Rooms whose use is fixed by furniture. Corridors, foyers and stairs are judged by circulation; a car bay by its statutory 3 x 6 m; a store or balcony has nothing that must fit.

grading.source: Practice. Within 50 mm a room is furnished: these clearances are conventions, not tolerances anyone builds to, and a dining room 1 cm short of one is not a finding. A foot is the difference between a bed with a way round it and a bed pushed into a corner, or a kitchen with a working aisle and one you edge along. Short by less, the room works with a tighter clearance: minor. Short by more, the furniture it exists for does not go in: major.

master_bedroom.holds: a double bed with a way round it and a wardrobe

arrangements.name: wardrobe facing the foot of the bed

along.for: passage at the foot, wardrobe doors open

arrangements.name: bed against a side wall, wardrobe facing its open side

across.for: bedside, standing at the open wardrobe

master_bedroom.source: Practice. 600 mm to get out of bed on either side, 750 mm to walk past the foot and open a wardrobe. The second arrangement is how a 10 x 10 ft room is actually furnished: one side of the bed against the wall, which is tight and livable. The same furniture as any bedroom: a master bedroom's extra size is its target area, not a different minimum use.

bedroom.source: Practice. A double bed, not a single: in an Indian house the second bedroom is as often a couple's or a parent's as a child's, and a room sized for a single bed cannot be changed later.

hall.holds: a sofa, a coffee table and a TV wall with a way past
hall.source: Practice. A three-seat sofa is 2.1 x 0.85 m; seated viewing across a coffee table needs about 1.75 m to the TV unit; the way through a living room runs beside the sofa, not between it and the TV.

dining.holds: a table for six with the chairs pulled out
dining.source: Practice. A six-seat table is 1.8 x 0.9 m, and a chair needs 750 mm behind the table edge to be pulled out and sat in. Six rather than four because the household this product serves eats together, joint families included.

kitchen.holds: a counter with a working aisle and a fridge
kitchen.source: Practice. 600 mm modular counters, a 1.0 m aisle between them — two people pass, an oven door opens — and room for a fridge. A single-wall galley narrower than this is a corridor with a counter in it, and stretching the work triangle along a 4.7 m strip is what the JP Nagar kitchen did.

bathroom.holds: a WC, a basin and a shower, each with room to use it

across.for: standing in front of the fixtures

bathroom.source: Practice. The three fixtures ⑥ draws in a bathroom, in a row, with 200 mm either side of the WC and 600 mm to stand in front of them — the 5' x 7' bathroom Indian builders call standard.

pooja.holds: a mandir shelf and room to sit before it
pooja.source: Practice. A 450 mm shelf and room for two people to sit in front of it.
